check-items.comment: Checks, each a name with its arguments; `!` before one drops it from the defaults of a wider scope.

check-declaration.comment: `check name(params): command`: a test of one artifact, which reads `{@path}` and each `{param}`. A step's product named `check` takes `=`, so it is not one.

review-declaration.comment: `review name`: a judgement a person makes, with no parameters and no command. A step's product named `review` takes `=`, so it is not one.

review-default.comment: `default review: looked_at, !other`, or `review:` in a `default:` block: the reviews that judge every output of a file or stage. A step's product named `review` takes `=` outside parentheses, so it is not one.

review-file.comment: `review looked_at from qc/looked_at.csv`, in a recipe: the file a review's verdicts are in.

review-clause.comment: `@review(looked_at)` on a source, a port or an output, with its keyword directly after the `@` as SPIT reads it.

review-items.comment: Reviews, each a name; `!` before one drops it from the defaults of a wider scope.

patterns.comment: `source_paths:` in a .spitout: each indented `source: path` line is a source path rule, which may hold shapes.

stage-header.comment: `stage name:` opens a stage; its lines are indented beneath it.

patterns.comment: SPIT fills placeholders in double quotes; single-quoted text is literal, as in Bash.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.spit

input-header.comment: A .spitin names its pipeline; pipelines, recipes and saved inventories can name a dataset root and an output root. `root` and `output` are reserved, so a line starting with either is that keyword, though a .spitout record may still be called `root[...]` or `output[...]`; `pipeline` is no keyword of a pipeline, so a product may take its name.

keyword-blocks.comment: A keyword alone with its `:` opens a block of its statements, each written on a line indented beneath it without the keyword. The block ends at the first line with code that is indented no further than the keyword.

patterns.comment: `source:`: a source on each line beneath it, written without `source`.
`operation:`: an operation on each line beneath it, written without `operation`; one ending in `:` holds its body.
A many input's minimum, `items: many Image @min(2)`, matched whole so the `)` of `min(2)` does not end the inputs.
A `+` that appends a `beside` suffix to the whole file name: `bai: Bai +.bai beside bam`, `+"_index.txt"`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.append.spit

patterns.comment: A `/` that makes the output a folder, alone or after its extension: `-> (subject: FsSubject /)`, `-> Zarr .zarr/`.
patterns.name: constant.other.extension.folder.spit

patterns.comment: The extension the tool gives an output's file: `-> Transform .mat`.
patterns.name: constant.other.extension.spit

patterns.comment: A `+` that appends a `beside` suffix to the whole file name: `bai: Bai +.bai beside bam`, `+"_index.txt"`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.append.spit

patterns.name: constant.other.extension.folder.spit

patterns.comment: The extension the tool gives an output's file: `-> Transform .mat`.
patterns.name: constant.other.extension.spit

patterns.comment: `command:`: an operation's command on each line beneath it, `name: program ...`, which may go on over lines indented further; an entry `name:` alone holds its lines beneath it, run in order.
`command name:` with nothing after its `:`: a command on each line beneath it, run in order; a line indented further goes on with the line above.
`verify:`: an operation's `verify` command on each line beneath it.
`resources:`: what each job of an operation needs on each line beneath it, `name: cores=8, memory=16G`.
`check:`: a check on each line beneath it, `name(params): command`.
`path:`: a product's path rule on each line beneath it, `product: template`.
`require:` in a recipe: a coverage rule on each line beneath it, written without `require`.
`exclude:` in a recipe: an exclusion on each line beneath it, written without `exclude`.
`dimensions [...]`: the order every product's dimensions follow.
`type Name<Param, ...>`: declares a parameterized type and names its parameters.
`types strict` or `types standard`: how much of the pipeline must be typed.
`command name: program ...`: the rest of the line is read as any other, apart from a `<` or `>` that connects the command's stdin or stdout.
`resources name: cores=8, memory=16G`: what each job of an operation needs.
`default:`, which opens a block of defaults.
`default ext:`, or `ext:` in a `default:` block: the extension a default path is completed with.
`default check:`, or `check:` in a `default:` block: the checks every output in a file or stage runs.
`path product:`, or `default path:` and `path:` in a `default:` block, then a template.

check-clause.comment: `@check(nonempty, ndim(3))` on a source or a port, ended at the end of the line so an unclosed one does not colour what follows, with its keyword directly after the `@` as SPIT reads it. An output may opt out of a default check with `!name`.

check-arguments.comment: The parameters of one check, such as the `3` of `ndim(3)`; they may nest.

patterns.comment: `default entities:`, or `entities:` in a `default:` block: the spelling of `{@entities}`, `{@key}` and `{@value}` joined by the text `separated` names.
`default entities sub: subject`: the label a dimension takes in that spelling.
A many input's minimum, `items: many Image @min(2)`, matched whole so the `)` of `min(2)` does not end the inputs.
A `+` that appends a `beside` suffix to the whole file name: `bai: Bai +.bai beside bam`, `+"_index.txt"`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.append.spit

patterns.comment: A `/` that makes the output a folder, alone or after its extension: `-> (subject: FsSubject /)`, `-> Zarr .zarr/`.

product-declaration.comment: A record of a source with no dimensions, such as `testset`, alone on its line.

invocation.comment: A step: its outputs, then the operation it calls, which an import may qualify, as `m, t = L::summarise(`.

inventory-entry.comment: A record; its source's path rule gives its file.

word-comment.comment: As in SPIT, `#` starts a comment only at the start of a word.
word-comment.name: comment.line.number-sign.spit

patterns.comment: `[[` and `]]` are literal brackets.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.bracket.spit

patterns.comment: `[...]`: part of a path a product keeps only when each placeholder in it has a value.
patterns.name: punctuation.definition.optional.spit

patterns.comment: SPIT's own placeholders, which take `@` to tell them from dimensions.

A dimension with a shape, `{date:date}`, `{run:digits}`, `{year:year}`: it narrows what a source's placeholder matches. Shapes belong to path rules and `discover` patterns only; a `command` line's `{x:date}` is something else, and takes the generic placeholder.
A dimension of the product.

resource-settings.comment: `cores=8` and `memory=16G` on a `resources` line: a job's cores, and its memory with a unit, K, M, G or T.

command-redirect.comment: A `<` or `>` that is a word of its own in an operation's command: `< {input}` reads an input on the command's stdin, and `> {output}` writes its stdout to an output. Quoted, either is an argument, and a string takes it first.
command-redirect.name: keyword.operator.redirect.spit

patterns.comment: `{image.dir}` and `{image.stem}`: an output's folder, and its file name without its extension. `{@output.dir}` and `{@output.stem}` are the unnamed output's.
`{durations.digit}`: each of an input's artifacts' value of a dimension. Any name after the `.` but `dir` and `stem`, which the pattern before takes.

`{@output}`, the path of an operation's single unnamed output, `{@cores}`, the cores its `resources` line gives each job, and `{@here}`, the folder of the file declaring it, and `{@path}`, the artifact a `check` tests; the `@` marks a placeholder SPIT supplies.
A source companion's suffix and `beside`, an extension with an optional `+` that appends it to the whole name: `source gps : Track .gpx beside raw`, `source fai : Fai +.fai beside reference`.
A source companion's quoted suffix and `beside`: `source mask "_mask.nii.gz" beside image`, `source dict +"_dict.txt" beside reference`.
A `/` that makes a source a folder, alone or after its extension: `source dicom : Dicom / [sub]`, `source store .zarr/`.
patterns.name: constant.other.extension.folder.spit

patterns.comment: The extension a source declares, before its dimensions or at the end of its line: `source events : Events .tsv [sub]`, `source gps : Track .gpx`.
patterns.name: constant.other.extension.spit
keyword.other.selector.spit
patterns.comment: A clause keyword directly after its `@`, as SPIT reads it: `@vary(`, not `@ vary(`.
